kiln_p15_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_001.text: Jian asked Yue to sit behind him when the reviewer opened the new account. Peng attended to preserve the agreed record, while a separate apprenticeship representative explained the review process in ordinary terms. The boy could correct his statement, ask for clarification and decline guesses about things he did not remember. Nobody promised a light consequence for speaking. Nobody demanded a particular confession to end the uncomfortable night. Yue watched his fingers flatten the district desk answer against the table. The paper had reached him before his hoped-for emergency could make its ordinary path seem impossible.

kiln_p15_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_002.text: He began with the sentence he had said by the bakery: he had not wanted Han burned. The reviewer asked what act he was describing. Jian said he had removed the stop pin and put a small wedge in the vent frame. The room went still. He named the common gripping tool and the scrap shelf where he had cut the wedge earlier. He had intended a narrow opening that would produce a visible process fault. He had not been authorised to alter the live vent. The words arrived slowly, each one making an imagined enemy become a person's decision.

kiln_p15_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_003.text: The reviewer asked for the sequence without offering the findings as answers. He left the documentation bench under the unassigned chalk explanation, took the tool and went to the passage between operator checks. The pin resisted at first. He turned it with the tool and held the shutter against the gust while inserting the wedge. When he let go, the shutter moved farther than his imagined gap. He stepped back rather than remain to restore it. He returned the tool near his bench before the warning sequence began. Yue could barely look at the hands that had done those movements.

kiln_p15_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_004.text: He described the place where he put the pin beneath the receiving cloth. Its position matched the recorded find. The wedge's shape and material matched the common scrap selection he named. His tool account fit the jaw comparison and access history. The operator's verified earlier check and the witness change bounded the time. Those independent details corroborated the confession without making it the only evidence in the room. Peng read the sequence back and asked him to correct anything uncertain. He changed the order of one small movement and left the uncertain interval unnumbered.

kiln_p15_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_005.text: Jian said he thought a slight opening would chill part of the shelf, spoil some ware and stop the firing safely at comparison. He had heard the cold model lesson about combustion, draft and hot grit. The reviewer asked why he believed he could control a live condition beyond his qualification. He looked down at the desk answer. He had imagined the wedge would hold the small gap, and the warning system he helped study would catch any change. Knowing danger existed had not made his private plan safe; it had made him believe he could arrange the danger's size.

kiln_p15_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_006.text: He wanted the district team to inspect the workshop now, not later in summer. He believed a visible fault would bring someone outside the owner's chosen teachers, and that person would hear the unresolved apprenticeship questions. The urgent visit had arrived, but it concerned the active hazard he created. It did not automatically become the general review or a certificate. The reviewer made that consequence plain. Yue heard the boy's assumption fail in the same room as his act became known. A fire could compel attention and still fail to compel the particular answer its author wanted.

kiln_p15_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_007.text: Peng placed the earlier interim submission and acknowledgment beside the desk answer. The ordinary review had been moving before the vent report. Jian said the answer was too small. It did not show how tired learners became. The apprenticeship representative agreed that a desk review could not replace every observation. It could answer some questions and preserve others for the visiting team. The limits were real. They did not establish that creating a live hazard was the only route to being heard. The boy cried at the distinction he could now explain and had refused to believe.

kiln_p15_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_008.text: Yue wanted to comfort him and felt anger rise instead. He had used the warnings that workers trusted as part of his imagined safe stunt. He had counted on Luo, Han and the crew to catch a danger they had not chosen. She said this when invited to describe the conversations she witnessed. She shook. She kept the fire question, inspection worry and explicit refusal in their actual order. Jian looked toward her as though friendship should make the account softer. She remained behind his chair and told the truth there rather than leave him alone.

kiln_p15_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_009.text: The reviewer established the current supported act and motive provisionally, subject to formal hearing and corrected evidence. Jian's live fixture access remained suspended. Ordinary paid cold duties could continue under a safe defined arrangement while the apprenticeship consequence was reviewed. The actual injury, ware loss and user delay would be included, not reduced to a successful inspection request. His previously demonstrated skills remained historical facts. They would not become never learned; they also would not excuse the deliberate alteration. Yue found the separation painful and necessary. Accountability could keep a learner's whole history without making all of it equally innocent.

kiln_p15_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_010.text: After the account, Jian sat in the empty visitor passage with his face in his hands. Yue offered water and waited for him to take it. He asked whether she hated him. She said she was angry and frightened by what he had chosen, and still there. He wanted a simpler answer. She could not give one without lying about either the burn or their winter. His ordinary nineteen years did not make the act childish in its consequences. It did make her see a person who would have to live beyond this room if anyone let him learn how.

kiln_p15_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_011.text: He said the loudest people always received the fastest response. Yue answered that he had made one of those loud responses by putting quieter people at risk. Han had not asked to become proof. The farmer waiting for seed jars had not asked to enter his argument with the district. Jian flinched at the concrete names. He had pictured a faulty kiln, a stopped schedule and an inspector, not a worker's sleeve edge or a cooperative's sacks. The real world filled the spaces his imagined mechanism had left blank. Yue let him see it without inventing an additional disaster.

kiln_p15_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_012.text: He asked to visit Han immediately. The clinician and Han would decide whether the visit suited his current care and wishes. An apology was not a key that opened another person's recovery room on demand. Jian accepted the answer and wrote a short offered message with Peng's help: the act, the known harm, no request for forgiveness. Yue did not write it for him. He needed his own ordinary words, clumsy enough to reveal he was not performing the perfect sentence a wiser friend could supply. The message waited until Han chose whether to receive it.

kiln_p15_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_013.text: Han read the offered note at the low clinic bench. He asked for the corroborated operational finding before deciding on a conversation. The owner supplied the permitted account, keeping unrelated private family letters out. He stared at the pin sequence and said very little. Yue sat beside him only after he asked. She wanted to explain Jian's desire for inspection. Han said he already understood the desire from the words. Understanding did not make his arm less tender. He needed time to be angry before anyone invited him to become the story's forgiving ending.

kiln_p15_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_014.text: Yue nodded and apologised for arriving with an explanation where he had asked for company. Han accepted the apology and asked about her own delayed anterior session. She said it would resume after the actual recovery conditions returned, not to escape the current hearing. He called that an inconveniently sensible plan. The old humor appeared for a moment and disappeared again when his dressing pulled. They sat through the change without making it mean he had either forgiven or withdrawn all friendship. A wounded person could have several ordinary moods in the same afternoon.

kiln_p15_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_015.text: Tan heard the corroborated account through the appropriate crew update. He looked sickened that Jian's vent plan resembled his own earlier habit of making a wished-for resource exist before asking the proper question. He did not claim equal intent or consequence. He said the shared error was expecting other people's competent work to rescue an unauthorized shortcut. Yue thought the comparison useful because it did not compete over who was better. Tan would answer the actual hearing questions about observed time and receiving work. His old fuel act remained its own record, neither cause nor excuse for Jian's choice.

kiln_p15_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_016.text: Luo met Jian separately with the representative present. He said the public inspection concern had been heard and submitted through an actual path. The deliberate live alteration broke a control boundary the boy understood. Further training would require a decision about trust, safety and roles, not only completed technical exercises. Jian asked whether learning the mechanism had made the foreman responsible. Luo said teaching carried duties, which the record would review. It did not remove the learner's agency after explicit scope and danger had been explained. The hard answer kept the boy a person, not a helpless instrument of instruction.

kiln_p15_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_017.text: The foreman then admitted his own failures: informal credit descriptions during winter, poorly protected warning arrangements and a hall that had relied too much on unwritten familiarity. Those matters remained real even after Jian committed a deliberate act. They would be part of the general review, with improvements already recorded. He would not erase them to make the boy the workshop's only problem. Jian looked up . Yue saw his fear that truth would become a weapon aimed one way. The shared account did not absolve him. It made the room large enough to hold more than his guilt.

kiln_p15_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_018.text: Peng closed the provisional packet with evidence and corrections intact. The formal hearing would consider the act, injury, material loss, public concern and consequence. Until then, the cold roster and fixture hold kept actual work safe. Yue finished the day's small index task and went upstairs with no appetite for a heroic cook's neat ending. Her friend had wanted the world to listen. He had made a dangerous statement with an ordinary wedge. The answer would require more than a loud punishment or a warm apology. It would require the people left afterward to find a truthful way to work.

kiln_p15_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_019.text: That night she dreamed of the shutter moving after Jian let go. The dream put her beside it with a third route that could hold any weight. She woke ashamed of the impossible rescue her sleeping mind had offered. The actual return had moved a quarter useful unit in a guarded task; it had never been a shield against hot grit or another person's choice. At breakfast she told Luo she had slept badly. He moved the session without fuss. The finite practice allowance remained available for a later recovered day. Losing a morning was smaller than lying about readiness.

kiln_p15_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_020.text: Zhu came down carrying a tray of uneven practice bowls. She had not yet heard all of the account and asked before repeating a rumor from the trimming room. Peng gave the crew's permitted summary. Zhu set the bowls down too carefully. She had spent years asking someone to admit that her completed work was real. Hearing that Jian had endangered another worker to force a similar acknowledgment felt like having her own claim dragged through a furnace. She said the resemblance did not belong to him alone. Nor did it make her wish to stand beside his act.

kiln_p15_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_021.text: Jian's mother arrived two days later after a runner found her at a cloth stall beyond the south road. Yue had heard her described as fierce and imagined a woman who would shout at every authority in the yard. She came in a rain-dark cape, asked whether her son was eating, and then asked to see the reviewed account. She read slowly. Nobody hurried the line where he had left the shutter after it overtravelled. When she looked up, her face had changed without becoming the simple face of either blame or protection.

kiln_p15_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_022.text: She asked whether he had been ordered to use the vent. The account and the operator roster answered no. She asked whether the common tool had been locked away. It had not, because ordinary cold workers needed it; access to a tool did not authorise a live alteration. The question was recorded as part of the hall's control review. She asked about Han's care. Peng showed the owner's funded arrangement and the limits of what could be shared. The mother nodded, gripping the cape cord so tightly that Yue watched the fiber whiten against her thumb.

kiln_p15_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_023.text: When she saw Jian, she slapped neither his face nor the table. She said he had once cut a hole in a grain sack because he wanted to discover why the patched cloth leaked. He had been seven, the sack empty, and she had made him sew the hole before dinner. He tried to smile at the old story. She said the empty sack had been his to handle. The live kiln and the people beside it were not. The memory became a measure rather than an excuse. He bent his head over her ordinary hands.

kiln_p15_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_024.text: Her stall had earned too little that winter. Jian had exaggerated his likely qualification date in letters because he wanted her to imagine a steadier income. She had repeated the date to a cousin who knew a pottery household. The promise had returned to him as a possible position he was not yet eligible to fill. None of that appeared in the operational finding as a hidden order to sabotage. It explained the pressure he had added to his own apprenticeship worry. Yue recognized the shame of making a hopeful sentence sound already earned, then living beneath it.

kiln_p15_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_025.text: The mother asked if he could remain employed. The owner could offer the currently safe cold duties while the hearing decided fixture access and the apprenticeship remedy. She would not promise lifelong employment in exchange for a confession. Nor would she charge his mother for damaged pots through an invented family debt. Actual responsibility would be decided with the applicable workshop rules and civil process. The mother listened without relief arriving all at once. A defined wage for the next week could buy food. It could not tell her what the boy would become afterward.

kiln_p15_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_026.text: Before leaving, she asked Yue whether her son had been kind to her. Yue answered with the good things she had actually known: careful archive copies, laughter during her painful recovery, carrying a tray at a height she could reach. The mother wept at those facts more than at the earlier account. She said people might now tell the story as though kindness had never existed. Yue said she would keep both truths. She would not make the good moments into permission, and she would not erase them to make the dangerous act easier to describe.

kiln_p15_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_027.text: Han chose to receive Jian's apology the following afternoon with a care worker nearby and no general audience. Yue waited outside. The boy entered with empty hands; a gift would have made the meeting resemble a purchase before either person spoke. He returned looking hollow and said Han had asked him to repeat the exact act without calling it a demonstration. Jian had done so. Han had told him he did not yet know whether he wanted future friendship. The answer was neither forgiveness nor a permanent verdict. Jian had to carry its uncertainty himself.

kiln_p15_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_028.text: Han later told Yue that the boy had cried and listened. He had not demanded that Han recognize the district worry before recognizing the burn. That mattered, though it did not solve the immediate difficulty of sleeping without catching his dressing. He wanted the clinic pots remade because his younger sister worked in that clinic and would otherwise hear the story through missing stock. He did not want her asked to defend his generosity. Yue wrote down the material need for the owner and kept the private family feeling out of the public loss list.

kiln_p15_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_029.text: The retained fragments became the next uncomfortable task. Peng asked Yue to help make an accurate failure record for the affected load. The damaged seed jar with a cold crack was ordinary ware made from a qualified body; its failure did not prove the body had always been unsuitable. The roughened clinic pot beside the hotter zone had a different damage pattern. They mapped each position against the firing slate and interrupted comparison readings. Yue had wanted these fragments to condemn a person. Their actual use was to explain a changed process without inventing a material fault.

kiln_p15_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_030.text: Zhu examined the rims with her good hand and supported the other at the bench. She distinguished an old trimming nick from a fresh thermal crack. One jar had been marked for ordinary rejection before loading; it could not join the claimed loss as though Jian had destroyed a finished sale. The owner struck it from the incident count. Jian watched this correction from the doorway of his cold task room. Yue saw surprise on his face. Accuracy protected him at a small point without declaring him innocent. The record did not need to become harsher than the real event.

kiln_p15_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_031.text: The cooperative customer brought a sack to show the jar capacity she needed. She had no interest in the workshop's dramatic account until she knew when her dry seeds could be stored. The owner offered the remaining accepted jars now, smaller approved temporary containers for the shortage, and the remade balance after the controlled firing could resume. The customer asked who would pay for an extra cart journey. The owner would, within the amended settlement. Yue found the modest question more revealing than another speech. Consequences arrived as ordinary hours and wheels long after the visible alarm stopped.

kiln_p15_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_032.text: At the receiving gate, Tan arranged those cart journeys with the agreed carrier and retained the actual quoted cost. His earlier private resource exchange made every new line feel watched. He did not try to regain comfort by becoming excessively strict with the customer. He asked the practical questions, sent the proposal for joint approval and waited. When it returned, the signature limits remained intact. Yue admired the plain work because it did not advertise itself as redemption. The dangerous shortcut had been quick. Its opposite looked like waiting beside a gate with a muddy wheel and an honest price.

kiln_p15_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_033.text: Jian's proposed cold work included sorting retained ordinary samples, cleaning removable uncharged shelves and copying corrected apprenticeship tasks. Luo excluded the live vent passage and hot loading area. The boy asked to make the improved stop retainer as a way of repairing what he had done. The reviewer refused to let the proposed remedy become access to the same fixture before the decision. He could prepare a cold sketch if he wished; qualified staff would design and install the working part. Remorse did not supply the missing authority. Jian accepted the copying task with a face that showed the cost.

kiln_p15_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_034.text: Yue helped him begin the archive list only after Peng approved the limited assignment and a second copy check. The room beneath the stairs smelled of paper, dust and ordinary clay. Jian read an old entry describing a trainee's dropped shelf as if it might show the future. That learner had completed a later safe course; another damaged entry gave no outcome. The archive was not a collection of guaranteed recoveries. Yue said they needed to preserve that uncertainty too. A true failed trial could teach without promising that every person who failed would be welcomed back.

kiln_p15_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_035.text: The boy found a sentence in his own earlier copy that called the ward signal a safeguard against all unexpected movement. He had written it as a summary of the warning lesson. The actual instruction named specific conditions and a response delay, not every motion. Peng checked the original and marked the copy's overstatement. It had not authorised his act, but it showed how a wish could enter a record through a confident paraphrase. Jian replaced it with the bounded description and retained the first wording beside the correction. Yue felt the lesson extend beyond his particular shame.

kiln_p15_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_036.text: In the next apprenticeship meeting, Zhu asked why learners had been expected to infer the difference between paid ordinary labor and assessable practice from other people's habits. Her own retrospective credit repair had revealed the weakness. Peng brought the task forms already in use, then asked learners to point out where they still confused wages, attendance and demonstrated skill. The meeting became noisy and useful. Jian was allowed to submit a written question through his representative but did not chair it. His act bought no leadership. The original public concern could still improve without rewarding the hazard he created.

kiln_p15_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_037.text: One younger learner said that everyone understood the forms now. Zhu asked him to explain the cooling comparison task to an imaginary worker arriving tomorrow. He described a teacher's glance as certification. The room laughed until it saw the error. Peng corrected the difference between permission to attempt, observed completion and recorded assessment. Yue remembered her own pleasure at hearing a new route named before she could use it. A title could arrive sooner than the capacity it seemed to promise. She wrote the three distinctions in her private notes as a lesson for any future pupil she might accept.

kiln_p15_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_038.text: Luo attended the second half of that meeting. He did not pretend that a clearer form could prevent every deliberate breach. He asked learners what practical routes remained when a supervisor failed to answer. The apprenticeship representative explained the alternate contact, preserved copies and review date. The owner agreed to paid time for supported submissions within a defined monthly allowance. Real hazards still used immediate warnings. Nobody needed to make a hazard to use the general path. Yue saw Jian hear the sentence from the doorway. It landed gently only because the room had first admitted its own imperfect history.

kiln_p15_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_039.text: The repaired cold retainer passed dimensional checks, then its guarded load comparison within the rated vent range. Jian was not present at the live check. The qualified operators worked from the revised procedure while the reviewer observed the boundary and warning response. The kiln did not earn a certificate for every future weather condition. It regained permission for the current defined ordinary schedule, with checks at each firing and a separate review for changed conditions. Yue watched the first flame through the safe observation opening and felt neither celebration nor dread alone. Useful work had returned with a visible edge.

kiln_p15_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_040.text: Han came as far as the cold boundary to see the restarted process. His care worker had cleared a short walk, not a return to the hot post. He kept his forearm away from the crowd and asked about the new retainer. Luo showed a duplicate rather than take him near the active fitting. Han said the duplicate looked unromantic. The foreman called that one of its virtues. Yue laughed and then stopped when she realized laughter did not require Han to be fully recovered. An injured worker could prefer an ordinary joke while still needing another dressing that evening.

kiln_p15_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_041.text: The first remake shelf held fewer pieces than the old production plan allowed. The owner accepted it to avoid crowding temporary storage and preserve comparison space. Customers received the revised delivery dates before the firing, not after a second failure. Yue used the cooler morning to carry light packing cloth below shoulder height. Her muscles felt eager to do more, the dangerous impatience of recovered confidence returning ahead of every clearance. She asked the clinician about the next gradual work step. The answer concerned a supported low lift in a separate review, not a heroic return during a shortage.

kiln_p15_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_042.text: That review took place with no burning kiln in view. Yue lifted a small weight from waist level to the permitted shelf, lowered it and reported the pull honestly. The clinician stopped the next heavier attempt when fatigue changed her motion. Her injury was recovering; she was not yet cleared for high sudden catches. Luo kept the planned anterior session separate from this physical work assessment. A route task and a material load tested different things, even when both used the same person. Yue disliked needing two answers and was relieved that one success could not conceal the other limit.

kiln_p15_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_043.text: After a quiet night, she returned to the anterior paired task at the previously recovered half-unit input over four ordinary breaths. The useful quarter moved the small guarded comparison weight and returned to ground cleanly. She interrupted the second planned repetition before input because her stance felt uneven. Luo checked the floor block and found its removable support had shifted during ordinary cleaning. They restored it, checked the setup and deferred the repetition until she felt recovered. Nobody accused the block of sabotage. The recent deliberate act made suspicion easy; ordinary causation still deserved its own patient examination.

kiln_p15_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_044.text: Her next-day touch, grip and leg movement remained normal. The missed repetition stayed missed. Peng asked how many successful anterior tasks she had now performed; Yue counted only the recorded recovered ones. She did not add imagined capacity from the interrupted setup. Her usable reserve stayed below the agreed thirty-six after the sampling discharge, and compatible charge below the required ninety percent on the method. Luo used those facts to shape gradual training, not to shame her. She could already feel a third pair. She could not turn that feeling into the four-pair assessment by wanting the months to end.

kiln_p15_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_045.text: At supper, Jian asked whether cultivation records allowed failures to remain visible after a person advanced. Yue showed him the page with the stopped higher attempt and the later successful task. She had been tempted to copy only the clean passage when sending a summary. The complete page explained how the recovered limit had been found. He read it for a long time. Their situations differed: her supervised stop had respected the boundary he deliberately crossed. She said so without withdrawing the example. A person could learn from a different kind of failure if the difference stayed clear.

kiln_p15_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_046.text: He asked her to sit behind him at the hearing. She agreed, provided he understood she would answer truthfully. He said he now did. Yue believed his present effort and did not pretend she could guarantee every future choice. He asked whether she would speak to the family of the cooperative customer for him. She declined to carry an apology they had not requested. He could offer one through the agreed contact after the hearing. Friendship had become less convenient. It also felt less fragile, because it no longer depended on each person guessing which truths the other could bear.

kiln_p15_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_047.text: Zhu spent an evening preparing her own account for the public apprenticeship review. She included the old missing credit, the corrected assessment and the remaining unfinished final examination. She refused a suggestion that the recovered credit meant her claim was fully resolved. The current fair task forms mattered; the lost years still had consequences no new signature could repay completely. Yue helped copy the dates and then asked about Zhu's glaze study. The trimmer smiled for the first time that evening. An unanswered harm and a present pleasure could occupy the same page without one canceling the other.

kiln_p15_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_048.text: Peng's ledger now contained two sorts of authorship more honestly than before. Teachers signed what they had seen. Learners corrected what they had done. The owner named costs she had approved. The external reviewer named the reach of the finding. None made a universal account. Yue watched Peng leave a deliberate blank where a disputed interval remained unresolved. She had once believed an archive should be complete enough to end doubt. It could instead be reliable enough to show where doubt began, and useful enough that the next worker did not fill the blank with a convenient story.

kiln_p15_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_049.text: The potter who supplied the common scrap came to identify the wedge's wood. She was embarrassed that a discarded piece from her shelf had become evidence. The reviewer said the material itself had no defect that explained the act. The question was what Jian had made and where he had put it. Yue saw the woman relax a little, then ask whether the loose scrap bin should move away from the live passage. That practical improvement could be considered without pretending a tidier bin would have removed the boy's capacity to choose a dangerous alteration.

kiln_p15_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_050.text: A neighborhood storyteller offered Peng a polished account for the owner's notice: a wicked apprentice, an observant cultivator, a timely rescue. Peng declined it. Yue disliked how easily the proposed hero could replace her actual limited work. Han disliked the version in which his pain existed to reveal her courage. The storyteller complained that the verified notice lacked an ending. Tan asked him to print the return dates and safe collection arrangements instead. Customers needed those ordinary facts now. Anyone seeking a complete moral would have to wait longer than a corrected production schedule.

kiln_p15_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_051.text: Jian's mother heard that public version before the notice was corrected. She came to Peng trembling, convinced the owner had chosen to disgrace her household. Peng showed the actual signed notice and traced how an unsourced retelling had spread. The mother asked whether they could forbid every repetition. They could issue the accurate account and request correction; they could not promise control over every mouth in town. Yue helped her write the request without a threat. It would not erase the act. It could stop a made-up rescue and invented family motive from becoming the only story people heard.

kiln_p15_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_052.text: The following morning the storyteller printed the correction below his usual market jokes. It named the unsupported details without repeating them at greater length. Jian read it through the copying room window. He said it would have been easier if Yue really had stopped a great explosion. Then at least he could be useful as the villain in a grand tale. She said an ordinary dangerous act did not need to become spectacular to matter. He looked at the remake cart and understood some part of the answer. Those smaller losses would remain after readers forgot the dramatic notice.

kiln_p15_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_053.text: An older apprentice asked whether Jian's cold duties meant he was being allowed to escape punishment through wages. Peng explained the arrangement and pending decision. Work already performed was still payable. Safe employment pending review did not restore live access or guarantee final qualification. The older learner said he had been sent home without pay after an accidental break at another shop. His question opened an additional grievance that needed its own source record. Yue admired Peng for not dismissing it as an inconvenient comparison. The hall's response to one act could reveal other unfair practices without making them identical.

kiln_p15_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_054.text: The owner met the crew over the next pay slate. The care and remake costs would appear in the workshop's incident account, not disappear through a smaller wage pool. A learner asked whether a future bonus might nevertheless shrink. The owner could not promise a profit that did not exist. She could preserve contracted wages, disclose the actual cost and calculate any discretionary bonus under the published rule rather than invent a hidden punishment. Tan prepared the figures. People listened more closely to that plain distinction than to an earlier assurance that the workshop would take responsibility.

kiln_p15_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_055.text: Zhu told Yue the bonus answer sounded ugly enough to be trusted. She had heard many beautiful promises paid out of someone else's overtime. They walked to the drying shelves, where ordinary clay jars waited without knowing anything about the hearing. Zhu set one aside because its foot rocked. Yue asked whether the slight wobble mattered for seed storage. The trimmer filled it with the test weight and showed how a narrow bench made the instability visible. Some defects became dangerous only in a particular use. They agreed not to hide that use behind a general claim of harmlessness.

kiln_p15_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_056.text: Yue took the rejected jar to the archive with a use note. Its fault had nothing to do with the vent act, though both appeared in the same week's records. She almost placed it among the incident fragments because that shelf was nearest. Peng caught the mistake before the label was written. They laughed at the ordinary convenience that could have created a false association. Yue moved the jar to its trimming series. The archive asked for less haste than the busy yard rewarded. Its quiet arrangement could become a technical argument years after everyone forgot who chose the shelf.

kiln_p15_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_057.text: A district clerk requested a copy of the earlier unsupported commercial certificate during the hazard inquiry. Peng supplied its narrow finding with the date and context. She refused to label it evidence that the workshop habitually falsified every record. The clerk accepted the distinction and asked which current procedures had changed. Yue helped retrieve the independent sample limits and joint commercial cover approvals. Jian's act had become known in an institution with prior weaknesses and real corrections. Both mattered to the review. Neither supplied a shortcut from the existence of one wrong act to the identity of every other author.

kiln_p15_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_058.text: That afternoon a child waiting with the cooperative customer asked Yue if cultivators could hear lies in someone's breathing. Yue said no. She could notice tension like anyone else, and tension had many causes. The child seemed disappointed until she let him compare two ordinary cracked sample rims under the supervised cold display rule. One had a visible old nick; the other needed the position record to make sense. Evidence turned out to require less mysterious power and more interesting attention than he expected. Yue enjoyed teaching that little lesson without treating it as a certificate to teach higher methods.

kiln_p15_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_059.text: Peng later asked whether she wanted a paid place assisting the future public sample visit. It would involve ordinary cold examples and preparation, with a qualified craft teacher responsible for the practical explanation. Yue accepted the limited task for the stated hours. She did not agree to demonstrate new channels for an audience. The offer mattered because it recognized a useful ability she had developed while she could barely lift a tray. Cultivation had returned to her life without swallowing every other form of competence. She went upstairs pleased with a wage and a task fitting her present self.

kiln_p15_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_060.text: Before the hearing packet closed, the representative read Jian his corrected account once more. He changed no fact to make it gentler. He added that the crew had not asked him to create evidence and that he had heard Yue's refusal. The addition did not turn her into the authority who could have prevented him by speaking more firmly. It placed responsibility where his own words said it belonged. Yue signed only her witnessed passages. When she handed the pen back, he thanked her without asking whether thanks meant they could begin again. For now, the accurate account was enough.

kiln_p15_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_061.text: Before the hearing, rain broke against the lodging roof. Jian sat with his mother at the kitchen table, preparing clothes that would not make him look either falsely important or theatrically ruined. She repaired an old cuff rather than buy him a new robe. Yue helped wash the supper bowls and listened to the needle passing through cloth. Nobody offered the sentence that everything would be all right. The boy asked what he should call the vent act in front of the customers. His mother said to call it what he had done, and let them hear the rest afterward.

kiln_p15_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p15_062.text: Yue carried her own account upstairs. The wet season had reached the yard without announcing a clean new beginning. Her shoulder moved freely within its current limit, the anterior return felt quieter than a secret, and her friend would be judged for a real act the next day. These facts belonged to one life rather than three separate stories. She folded the account into her habitual pack beside her travel notes. At morning she would go to the ash yard, sit where Jian had asked, and help a difficult truth become work that people could use after the hearing ended.
